title: The Wrong Song
moral: True friendship means helping others succeed, even when no one notices our help.

pages.text:
The school assembly hall was full of children.

Class Five had to sing a welcome song for the guests. Sana stood in the front row, holding the lyric sheet tightly.

She had practised all week.

Her brother had practised with her at home too, though he kept singing the line "Welcome everyone" as "Watermelon everyone."

Sana had laughed so much she forgot the second verse.

Now, on stage, she felt nervous.

The music started.

The first verse went well.

Then the second verse came.

Sana opened her mouth.

Nothing came out.

Her mind had gone blank.

The children beside her kept singing, but Sana stood frozen. Her face became hot.

In the second row, Aditi noticed.

Aditi was not in the front. No one could see her clearly. But she remembered the words.

Softly, without making it obvious, she sang the line a little louder.

Sana heard it.

Her memory returned.

She joined in again.

The song ended beautifully. Everyone clapped.

After assembly, the teacher praised the front row.

"Well done, Sana," she said.

Sana smiled, but she knew what had happened.

At lunch, she found Aditi near the stairs.

"You helped me," Sana said.

Aditi shrugged. "Only a little."

"No," Sana said. "I was stuck. You saved me."

Aditi smiled. "Your face looked like my maths book."

Sana laughed. "That bad?"

"Worse," Aditi said.

The next day, Sana brought a small thank-you note.

It said: You sang from behind, but you helped me stand in front.

Aditi read it twice.

Then she folded it carefully and kept it in her pencil box.

That afternoon, when the hall was empty, Sana stood on the stage and looked at the second row.

She understood something important. Sometimes the person who saves the moment is not the person everyone sees.
